content.text: Built end-to-end paid subscription support: checkout, webhooks,
customer portal, and failed-payment handling. Shipped to production
18 days ago.
Onboarded our first 12 paying customers through this stack.
Decisions
Went with
stripe-checkout
hosted page instead of custom UI — saved ~5 days.
Single subscription tier for now (Pro $19/mo). Annual + team plans deferred.
Webhooks routed through
/api/stripe/webhook
with signature verification.
Failed payments retry 3× over 7 days, then downgrade to Free with email notice.
What didn't work
Tried building custom invoice generation early on — abandoned after realizing
Stripe's invoice API covers everything we need for $0 extra.
Logged as a Dropped action.
Open follow-ups
Set up dunning emails (currently using Stripe defaults — could be more on-brand)
Add tax handling once we expand to EU customers
Test SCA flow with real European cards

references.title: Interno: notas de comparación de herramientas

content.text: Spent the first 25 days proving I can actually show up 4×/week consistently before
increasing volume.
Closed when streak hit 3 weeks of full attendance with 0 zero-effort sessions.
Week structure
Monday — easy 5km
Wednesday — strength (45 min)
Friday — easy 5km or tempo (alternating weeks)
Sunday — long run (start at 8km, build slowly)
Insights from this base period
Morning runs work better than evening for me — heart rate noticeably lower at the same pace,
and I'm less likely to skip when it's the first thing I do.
Strength day is the keystone — when I miss it, my Friday run feels heavier and form drops.
Treating it as non-optional from now on.

content.text: Where I am
Hit 28km last week. One more week at 28-30km, then start adding intensity per the next
project. Knees feel fine, sleep is good, appetite is up. Right side of the rubber band.
Pace targets at this volume
Easy runs — 6:00-6:30/km (HR < 145)
Long Sunday runs — 6:15-6:45/km
Recovery — slower than 6:30/km, no shame in walking

projects.title: Añadir entrenamientos de tempo e intervalos

content.text: Adding speed work after building base. One tempo session and one interval session per week,
starting easy and building up to race pace efforts.
First tempo done last week (3×1km @ 5:30/km — felt sustainable).
First interval session done — short reps to introduce the system gently.
Working through Aula Internacional 4 (B2 level). One unit per week,
writing every exercise out by hand — slower but retention is much better.
Process per unit
Day 1: read the unit, do reading exercises
Day 2-3: grammar drills + listening
Day 4: writing exercises (free composition)
Day 5: review with flashcards from Anki
Halfway through. Subjunctive feels much more natural than 6 weeks ago.
Reported speech (unit 4) was the hardest so far.
